A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, despite the title and method renaming. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original multilingual mathematical and scientific evaluations, component ablations, OOD results, and empirical studies in Appendices A, E, and F.

after.justification: v3 retains the work's original evaluations and appendix experiments, including results for smaller models and analyses of ability-related neurons and tensors.

M1.justification: MAET is renamed MAEC, but neuron selection, sparse training, weight decomposition, tensor selection, and parameter combination remain unchanged in Equations 1–5 and Algorithm 1. The new checkpoint-use clarification agrees with v2's existing pseudocode.

E1.justification: The training corpus families, multilingual mathematical and scientific tasks, forum-corpus study, and OOD tests are retained. Chinese coverage remains documented in Appendix C and Tables 6 and 8 despite removal of its mixing-coefficient row.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds mathematical-task comparisons with GPT-3 175B, PaLM 62B, cont-PaLM 62B, and Flan-cont-PaLM 62B. Existing CPT, domain-adaptation, data-augmentation, and task-vector comparators remain, as do the appendix comparator sets.

E3.justification: Higher-is-better RICER is replaced by lower-is-better ICER, reported only for improving methods. Table 5 changes the mathematical tensor-selection ratio from 80% to 60%, although Appendix B still states 80%. This establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun. Dataset counts and training budgets otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, tensor-ratio sweep, OOD evaluations, and appendix empirical analyses retain the same evidence. The ablation and sensitivity figures are redrawn and renumbered; the added robustness discussion interprets the existing sweep rather than introducing another test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. Results remain point estimates, with averages across languages rather than reported run-to-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes F-CPTL&T's Telugu mathematical accuracy from 35.5 to 25.5 and its average from 37.3 to 34.0, reversing its ranking relative to the proposed method's retained 35.7. F-CPTL & DA's Bengali score changes from 34.4 to 30.4 and its average from 34.5 to 33.2. Added closed-source results and replacement efficiency scores further revise the comparisons. The ranking reversal materially changes evidence for the main mathematical-performance claim; appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal task setup, Equations 1–5, and mathematical content of Table 4 and Algorithm 1 are retained. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added. The ICER passage uses the cost/improvement expression already printed in v2, while changing its metric interpretation and reporting.

C1.justification: The abstract adds a claim of performance comparable with PaLM and explicitly identifies LLaMA-3 8B. Its earlier emphasis on baseline outperformance using 60% of the computational resources remains in the main text. The central contribution of extracting and combining abilities across languages is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly interprets the retained tensor-ratio sweep as evidence of robustness, highlighting mathematical performance near 35.5 for ratios 0.6–0.8. v2 emphasizes deterioration at extreme ratios. Table 3's caption also narrows the attribution of OOD degradation from previous methods generally to CPT specifically. The stated limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 clarifies the sampled corpus and checkpoint usage, and Appendix G/Table 9 explicitly summarizes baseline configurations. Table 5 revises tensor-ratio documentation and removes the previously supplied Chinese mixing coefficient of 2.0. Most hyperparameters, software information, the translation prompt, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chung et al. (2024) for the closed-source comparisons and Gafni and Birch (2006) for ICER, while removing several references, including QLoRA, prefix-tuning, ROOTS, and MetaMath. The positioning around continual pre-training, knowledge editing, and model merging remains substantially the same. The duplicated Cheng reference concerns an already cited work.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change from MAET/transfer to MAEC/combination, alongside condensation of the abstract, introduction, and related work. A metrics passage, acknowledgements, and Appendix G are added. The overall section organization remains intact, and the old MAET name persists in the conclusion and several appendix passages.

P2.justification: v3 adds an overview Figure 1 that redisplays selected existing results and a baseline-summary Table 9. Table 2 gains comparator-group headings; existing figures receive revised labels and captions, and the scientific sensitivity plot uses a wider vertical scale. Appendix tables are redistributed across pages without changing their retained results.

improvement.justification: v3 offers clearer checkpoint and baseline explanations and aligns the efficiency metric's name with its preferred direction. However, Table 5 newly conflicts with Appendix B over the mathematical tensor ratio, and the Chinese mixing coefficient disappears despite retained Chinese experiments. Table 2 also revises baseline scores without explaining the changes, including a consequential ranking reversal. These clarity gains and unresolved reproducibility and evidence issues prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
